title: Foundations review
focus: Revisit all 13 foundation skills in one mixed, 33-question review. Preparation is optional; save and resume whenever you need a break.

exercises.prompt: Which vowel group describes talo (“house”)?
exercises.explanation: The vowels a and o in talo are back vowels. The back-vowel group is a, o, u.

optionFeedback.front vowels: Front vowels are ä, ö, y. The a and o in talo belong to the back-vowel group.
optionFeedback.only neutral vowels: Only e and i are neutral. Talo contains a and o, which are back vowels.
optionFeedback.back vowels: Correct. Both a and o are back vowels.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: Vowel harmony: form not yet correct

exercises.prompt: hattu (“hat”) → ____ (“of the hat”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: The ending -n is supplied. Recall the weak stem: tt becomes t, giving hatu-. Add -n: hatun (“of the hat”).

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT double consonants: strong grade retained
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The ending is correct, but tt must become t: hatu- + n = hatun.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT double consonants: form not yet correct

exercises.prompt: tuoli (“chair”) → ____ (“chairs”)
exercises.explanation: tuoli means “chair”; tuolit means “chairs”. The nominative T-plural is formed here by adding -t: tuoli → tuolit.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Regular T-plural: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.explanation: In this taught T-plural, keep tuoli unchanged and add -t: tuolit.

exercises.prompt: pöytä (“table”) → ____ (“of the table”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: The ending -n is supplied. The single t changes to d: pöydä- + n = pöydän (“of the table”).

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT common single consonants: strong grade retained
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The ending is correct. Change t to d in the weak stem: pöydän.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT common single consonants: form not yet correct

exercises.prompt: they leave — use the supplied stem lähte- from lähteä (“to leave”)
exercises.explanation: lähteä means “to leave”; lähtevät means “they leave”. The stem lähte- is supplied. For he (“they”), vowel harmony selects -vät: lähtevät.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: Subject (who does it) + verb (what they do)

parts.role: Subject — the people doing the action.
parts.formation: he is already the basic pronoun meaning “they”, so it does not need an ending here.

parts.role: Verb — the action performed by the plural subject.
parts.formation: The exercise supplies the stem lähte-, so no stem-building rule is being tested. Add -vät; this ending shows that the subject is he (“they”). Vowel harmony chooses -vät because the supplied stem uses front vowels ä, ö, or y, or only neutral vowels e and i.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: Third-person plural -vat/-vät: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The supplied stem lähte- has ä and neutral e, with no back vowel. Use -vät: lähtevät.

exercises.prompt: puku (“suit”) → ____ (“of the suit”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: Recall the taught pair puku–puvun. Here k changes to v, giving puvu-. Add the supplied -n: puvun (“of the suit”). This is a learned special-k pattern, not a rule for every k.

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT special k changes: special weak stem missed
answerDiagnostics.explanation: For this taught word, use puvu-. Do not keep k or simply remove it: puvu- + n = puvun.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT special k changes: weak stem not yet correct

exercises.prompt: puisto (“park”) → ____ (“in the park”)
exercises.explanation: puisto means “park”; puistossa means “in the park”. The back vowels u/o select -ssa.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Inessive -ssa/-ssä: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The u and o in puisto require -ssa. Keep the stem unchanged: puisto + ssa = puistossa.

exercises.prompt: kampa (“comb”) → ____ (“of the comb”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: The ending -n is supplied. The cluster mp becomes mm: kamma- + n = kamman (“of the comb”).

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT consonant clusters: strong grade retained
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The weak stem has mm, not mp: kamma- + n = kamman.

exercises.instruction: Identify the consonant change in the supplied forms.
exercises.prompt: pankki (“bank”) → pankin (“of the bank”): which consonant change is shown?
exercises.explanation: Compare pankki with pankin. The double kk becomes a single k; the separate -n ending marks the genitive.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT recognition: form not yet correct

optionFeedback.k → ∅: One k remains in pankin. Here double kk becomes single k; a single k is not disappearing.
optionFeedback.kk → k: Correct. Pankki has kk and pankin has k.
optionFeedback.nk → ng: Pankin still has nk, not ng. The change is kk to k.

exercises.prompt: matto (“carpet”) → ____ (“of the carpet”)
exercises.explanation: Use the genitive ending -n and the weak stem mato-: tt becomes t, then mato- + n = maton (“of the carpet”).
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Genitive -n: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The genitive ending -n is right. Weaken tt to t before adding it: maton.
Matot means “carpets”. “Of the carpet” needs genitive -n: maton.

exercises.prompt: pelto (“field”) → ____ (“fields”)
exercises.explanation: pelto means “field”; pellot means “fields”. Add plural -t to the weak stem. The KPT change is lt → ll: pelto → pellot.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: T-plural with KPT: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.category: T-plural with KPT: strong grade retained
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Before plural -t, change lt to ll: pello- + t = pellot.

exercises.prompt: ____ ovat kotona. (“The pictures are at home.”) · use kuva (“picture”); kotona is supplied as “at home”
exercises.explanation: The subject is plural: kuva → Kuvat. A plural subject uses ovat, meaning “are”.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: Plural subject (who or what) + ovat (“are”) + place or state

parts.role: Subject — the people or things that the sentence is about.
parts.formation: Start with kuva. The stem stays unchanged. Add plural -t: kuvat.

parts.role: Verb — connects the plural subject to its place or state.
parts.formation: olla is the dictionary form meaning “to be”. Because the subject means more than one, use the third-person plural form ovat, meaning “they are”.

parts.role: Place or state — tells where the subject is or what its condition is.
parts.formation: kotona is supplied as a complete fixed word meaning “at home”. No place-ending rule is being tested.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: Plural subject + ovat: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.category: Plural subject + ovat: singular subject used
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The meaning “pictures” and the plural verb ovat need a plural subject. Add -t: Kuvat ovat kotona.

exercises.prompt: Which vowel group describes pöytä (“table”)?
exercises.explanation: All three vowels in pöytä, ö, y and ä, belong to the front-vowel group.

optionFeedback.back vowels: Back vowels are a, o, u. The dots distinguish ä and ö from a and o; pöytä has front vowels.
optionFeedback.front vowels: Correct. Ö, y and ä are all front vowels.
optionFeedback.only neutral vowels: Only e and i are neutral. Pöytä contains ö, y and ä, which are front vowels.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Keep the supplied -n, but weaken pp to p: lipu- + n = lipun.

exercises.prompt: poika (“boy”) → ____ (“of the boy”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: Recall the taught pair poika–pojan and the weak stem poja-. In this word, k disappears and i changes to j. Add the supplied -n: pojan (“of the boy”). Learn the whole pair; simply replacing k with j would give the wrong stem.

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT special k changes: special weak stem missed
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The taught weak stem is poja-, with oj rather than oi. Add the supplied -n to get pojan.

exercises.prompt: kirjasto (“library”) → ____ (“in the library”)

exercises.misconceptionCategory: Inessive -ssa/-ssä: ending not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The a and o determine harmony even though i is neutral. Use -ssa: kirjastossa.

exercises.instruction: Identify the consonant change in the supplied forms.
exercises.prompt: leipä (“bread”) → leivän (“of the bread”): which consonant change is shown?

exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT recognition: form not yet correct

optionFeedback.pp → p: Leipä has one p, not pp. Here the single p becomes v.

exercises.prompt: hatun — from hattu (“hat”)
exercises.explanation: Hatun is the genitive of hattu (“hat”). It means “of the hat” or “the hat's”: tt becomes t and the ending is -n. Finnish has no word corresponding to the English article here.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Genitive -n: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The ending is -n, which marks genitive here, not plural -t. Hatun means “of the hat”.
